title: Progressive stacking and microflow prioritization for Console billing & rollout panels on narrow viewports
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
The billing panel, rollout controls, and cost-explorer tables have divergent behavior at narrow widths and under touch/gesture-heavy environments. On smaller screens we currently collapse columns aggressively which breaks key microflows (switching rollout variants, quick cost pivots). There have been a handful of support tickets where customers could not complete a canary rollback on mobile/small window sizes.

Goals:
- Create a progressive stacking strategy for the billing/rollout surfaces such that critical actions remain visible and reachable at <= 480px width.
- Define microflow priority rules (which controls remain sticky, which collapse into overflow menus, which hide behind a Details drawer).
- Produce a small prototype (Figma + interactive HTML) that demonstrates table collapse, chart resizing, modal stacking, and scroll-lock behavior across Chrome, Safari (iOS), Firefox and Edge.
- Produce a cross-browser QA checklist and a set of acceptance criteria for Engineering to implement.

Scope & non-goals:
- Scope: Billing summary card, rollout action bar, primary cost-explorer table, compact chart thumbnails in the cost panel, modal stack behavior when the user opens a rollout modal from a table row.
- Non-goals: Full redesign of cost-explorer flows, backend changes, or changes to RBAC. This ticket focuses on client-side layout rules and interaction cadence only.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Prioritize action affordances: primary CTA (Rollback/Apply) must remain sticky in the rollout action bar; all secondary actions should collapse into a contextual menu when width < 560px. This preserves primary microflows.
- Use progressive disclosure for dense tables: collapse non-essential columns into a per-row Details drawer. Keep the key columns (name, cost delta, status) visible at all sizes.
- Chart thumbnails: fall back to sparkline-only view at narrow widths to reduce vertical scroll. Full chart appears in an overlay when tapped.
- Modal stacking behavior: when a modal opens from a narrow panel, soften the backdrop and animate an anchored sheet from the bottom (mobile pattern) preventing double-scroll and preserving keyboard focus.
- Cross-browser smoothing: avoid heavy CSS filters and focus on robust flex/grid fallbacks; explicit -webkit-overflow-scrolling for iOS momentum and detect passive event listeners for Safari to prevent jank.

Deliverables:
- Figma workfile with three breakpoints (>=1200px, 560-1199px, <=559px) and annotated interactions. (link below)
- Interactive prototype (small HTML/CSS/JS) demonstrating stacking, table collapse, modal sheet. (link below)
- Acceptance criteria and QA matrix.
- Component guidance for Engineering: CSS variables, token usage, transition durations, and ARIA behaviors for collapsible rows and modal sheets.

References and links:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/example/console-billing-stack (prototype frames: breakpoints + interactions)
- Quick demo HTML: https://redwood-internal.share/prototypes/295001/stacking-demo
- Related design ticket tracking: DES-41234 (elastic-panel-reflow)
acceptance_criteria: Primary rollout CTA remains visible and actionable at <=480px without horizontal scroll
Secondary actions collapse into a single overflow menu for widths < 560px
At <=480px the cost-explorer table hides non-essential columns and exposes a per-row Details drawer
Chart thumbnails degrade to sparklines; tapping opens full chart overlay without launching a new browser tab
Modal opened from a narrow panel presents as a bottom sheet, maintains focus, and prevents body scroll
Prototype demonstrates consistent behavior on Chrome (desktop & Android), Safari (iOS & macOS), Firefox, and Edge
Design handoff includes accessible ARIA patterns and a cross-browser QA checklist
comments: 2026-02-12 — Asha Patel: Initial brief added. Flagging existing support tickets (SUP-932, SUP-947) related to rollbacks failing on small screens. Assigned to Miguel for first-pass layouts.

2026-02-18 — Miguel Ortega: Pushed first Figma frames covering the three breakpoints. Noted a constraint: current table virtualization relies on fixed column widths; will need an engineering spike to make columns collapsible. Added spike request to ENG-1842.
2026-02-25 — Product Review (Lena Kim): Reviewed flows — emphasized that in rollback microflow we cannot hide the timestamp column; request to surface relative time in a compact form. Added as AC 3.

2026-03-02 — Accessibility (Vijay Rao): Confirmed ARIA approach for collapsible rows; recommended role=button on disclosure and focus management for bottom sheet. Suggested keyboard shortcut to open per-row Details for power users.

2026-03-05 — Engineering sync (Synthesis): Miguel, Ryan (ENG) and Asha aligned on solution: implement per-row Details as a lightweight overlay rather than re-rendering table; use CSS container queries for collapse thresholds; engineering to follow up in ENG-1842. Miguel to provide CSS tokens.

2026-03-10 — Design update: Prototype updated to include a compact 'cost delta' pill and icon-only action group at <=420px. Added prototype performance notes for Safari iOS where the pinned CTA caused layout reflow; swapped to transform-based animation which resolved jank in the demo.

2026-03-14 — PM review (Nora Jensen): Approved for implementation in Cycle 2026-W10; priority P1. PM requested telemetry hooks be added (event names) to track collapse usage and rollback success rates post-deploy. Added dependency PM-420 for telemetry tracking.
2026-03-14 — Next steps (Asha): Prepare handoff package (Figma, tokens, prototype, QA checklist) and schedule design pairing session with ENG during week of 2026-03-16.
